sentences.text: The premise is false on this record: fiscal 2026 free cash flow fell short of net income, so the claim fails as worded rather than on a technicality.
The shortfall is not a spending story, since capex stayed under 5% of revenue; it comes from receivables and inventory absorbing cash that net income counts but the cash flow statement does not.

The gap is widening, not closing: free cash flow as a share of net income has fallen at every 10-K reading, and over the four quarters to Q2 FY2027 the shortfall grew to $65.87B with conversion of 0.40x in the latest quarter alone.
That makes NVIDIA unusual against its industry: its cash conversion ranks 32 of 38 among SIC 3674 filers, while FCF above net income held in 116 of 179 company-years for those peers.

For a buy decision the step that matters is that the 2026-09-30 price, a 2.3% free cash flow yield, rests on earnings that are increasingly running ahead of cash, so the claim's failure weakens rather than supports the earnings-quality case for buying.

The reverse DCF assumes each dollar of new revenue needs capital at a sales-to-capital of 1.47; receivables and inventory rising faster than revenue is evidence that growth may tie up more capital than that assumption allows, which would raise the 13.4% growth the price needs.
In absolute terms the cash generation is still exceptional: free cash flow margin ranks 2 of 62 in the industry at 44.8%, so missing net income is a matter of conversion, not of weak cash.
Because capex is light, the gap sits almost wholly in working capital, which can unwind if receivables are collected and inventory is shipped, whereas a capex-driven gap would be structural.

Management attributes the rise in operating cash flow to higher revenue, consistent with receivables and inventory building in a period when sales were growing at +105.9% year over year in the latest quarter.
Even operating cash flow fell short of net income in fiscal 2026, so the failure does not depend on how capex is counted.
The trend runs one way across three 10-Ks and then sharpened in the trailing quarters, which argues against reading fiscal 2026 as a one-year timing blip.
Among filers with at least $100.00B of revenue, FCF above net income held in 48 of 83 company-years, so NVIDIA's position below the line is not explained by its size either.
Whether the receivables and inventory build reverses in coming quarters or keeps compounding, which the record cannot forecast; only later balance sheets will show it.

Whether customers are paying more slowly or the build reflects shipments in transit; the record gives the size of the build but no cause, and the filings' receivable aging or days-sales figures would be needed.
How much of the buy case leans on reported earnings, priced at 28.5x, rather than cash, since the two are diverging.

conditions.text: Accounts receivable falling below the $63.06B level of Q2 FY2027 would show the working-capital drag starting to unwind.
Inventory falling below the $31.57B level of Q2 FY2027 would release cash and narrow the gap to net income.
Quarterly free cash flow rising above the $21.40B of Q2 FY2027 would be a first sign conversion is recovering.
